hook: Traditional office chairs hide heavy metal boxes beneath the seat, but one new design throws them out entirely.

sections.voiceover: Traditional office chairs hide heavy metal boxes beneath the seat, but one new design throws them out entirely.
b_roll: Close-up of a standard mechanical chair mechanism underneath the seat
Cut to the minimalist profile of the new chair

sections.voiceover: At ORGATEC in Cologne, German brand Wilkhahn revealed the WiChair task chair. Designed by Alina Schnizler, the frame swaps levers for spring-loaded steel and plywood. Where is the heavy mechanism?
b_roll: Exhibition hall floor at ORGATEC in Cologne showing Wilkhahn displays
Spring-loaded steel swing arm flexing under pressure

sections.voiceover: Wilkhahn's dynamic sitting legacy began with the 1980 FS-Line release.
b_roll: Archival product photograph of the FS-Line office chair from 1980

sections.voiceover: Following the Picto model in 1992 and the ON chair in 2009, this latest release eliminates mechanical clutter. A single springy steel swing arm creates movement.
b_roll: WiChair swing arm bending smoothly during a recline test

sections.voiceover: Alina Schnizler's minimalist WiChair design ditches traditional mechanical boxes.
b_roll: Wide shot of WiChair in a modern workspace
